Jordan (PM): Quick sync — we need a concise PRD for rate limits / quotas / billing semantics. Customers keep asking about per-project caps, soft vs hard limits, and how overages should bill. Who wants to take lead?
Anya (Product): I can draft. proposal: 1) API semantics (429 vs quota error), 2) metering events for billing, 3) admin UI for limits, 4) rollout criteria + telemetry.
Ravi (Eng Lead): Important: separate enforcement (fast path) from metering (billing path). Enforcement must be in the runtime so we don't overspend. Metering events can be async but must be reliable (idempotent).
Liz (Eng PM): Acceptance criteria idea: - 95th percentile latency increase < 5% with rate limiter enabled; - no billing discrepancies > 0.1% in first month; - UI shows real-time remaining quota within 15s.
Samir K: Edge cases: streaming and function-calls. If a stream is cut due to quota, how do we bill partial tokens? We should define "billable units = tokens generated" and allow partial-charge semantics with clear retry_after header.
Matt H: From prioritization: two phases — Phase 1 (must-have for GA): enforcement + metering events + basic admin UI + billing integration. Phase 2: soft limits, overage auto-billing, per-route quotas, usage forecasting.
Ravi (Eng Lead): Technical question: do we count cached responses against quota? For most customers caching should not count; but for auditability we need a flag on metering events: cached: true/false.
Anya (Product): Good call. In PRD we should list allowed metering dimensions: customer_id, project_id, api_key, model, route, cached, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, streaming=true/false.
Samir K: Example metering event shape (proto):
```
{ "event": "tokens.generated", "customer_id": "acct_123", "project_id": "proj_456", "api_key": "sk-...", "model": "gpt-x", "prompt_tokens": 34, "completion_tokens": 512, "cached": false }
```
OpsBot: deploy-bot posted: "rate-limiter v1 deployed to cluster-3 at 2025-11-18T14:22:03Z"
Liz (Eng PM): API error examples we should standardize in spec: 429 for rate-limited, 403 for account suspended, 402 for billing-required/over-limit (if we choose). Suggest schema:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700000000
{
  "error": { "type": "quota_exceeded", "message": "Project quota exceeded", "retry_after": 120 }
}
```
Jordan (PM): Decision needed: do we expose rate limit headers by default? I vote yes — it's helpful for client retries and backoff.
Matt H: Agree. Also we need metrics: tokens_billed_total, quota_violation_count, overage_amount (USD), rate_limit_429_count per project. Those feed pricing and rollouts.
Ravi (Eng Lead): Implementation notes: - Token counting must happen at output commit time for streaming; - Make metering idempotent via event_id; - Default quota windows: per-minute for rate limiting, per-month for billing.
Anya (Product): Launch criteria proposal: - PRD approved, e2e tests for enforcement + metering, billing connector tested end-to-end on staging, UI prototype in Console, doc + SDK examples. Target: ship to hosted API users in beta in 8 weeks.
Samir K: Edge-case: multi-API key aggregation. If a customer has both hosted and dedicated keys, how do we aggregate for billing? Need mapping layer: project_id -> billing_account_id. Include that mapping in spec.
Jordan (PM): Next steps: Anya drafts PRD with above sections and rough ACs. Ravi & Liz to review for implementation and UI constraints. Samir to add streaming billing rules. Matt to write rollout metrics list. Due: propose draft by EOD Friday (1759200000).
Anya (Product): I'll start the draft. tagging @Ravi @Liz @Samir @Matt for reviewers. :thumbsup:
